text:
incident-bot: SEV2: runtime-prod-09 flapping (OOM + CUDA driver errors). Auto-escalation triggered. Affected pool: kv-paged-allocators. 

maya: ack, I'm on it. grabbing logs from the node now.

raj: I'm watching the allocator metrics — fragmentation (free_slab_ratio) trending down, resident pages increasing. looks like slow crawl, hit OOM at ~13:42.

sophie: customer-facing telemetry: a handful of customers (~3) reported 502s on /v1/embeddings and increased tail latency on /v1/generate. ramp from 0.3% to 4.7% errors since 13:35 UTC.

maya: paste kubectl output: ```kubectl -n runtime logs runtime-prod-09 -c runtime```
maya: ```E0323 13:41:57 runtime.go:214] cuda: failed alloc 0x0 (out of memory)
E0323 13:42:01 allocator.go:112] pager: attempted allocate page for model-id=redwood-llama-13b, shard=7 -> alloc failed
--- end ---```

raj: seeing repeated `page_alloc: slab fragment too small` in allocator logs. page sizes piling up as many tiny free fragments.

leo: is there any recent change to our compacting heuristics? I don't see any rollouts in the last 24h. infra-bot: no deploys in prod since 13:00 UTC.

maya: initial mitigation steps I ran: 1) disabled auto-prefetch on node 09 (to reduce KV prefetch pressure) 2) forced a compaction pass on that node: `allocator ctl compact --target=90` (kicked off, running).

raj: compaction progress looks slow, but fragmentation delta stopped increasing after disable. still at ~78% free_slab_ratio (bad).

support-engine: customers affected: corp-eta (embedding batch jobs) and beta-scribe (chat infill timeouts). support sent notices and raised incident flag to SEV2.

sophie: can we failover traffic from runtime-prod-09? autoscaler suggests spare capacity in runtime-prod-12 and -15 but model pins may prevent immediate fallback for some customers pinned to dedicated variants.

maya: I'm shifting routing for non-pinned traffic off prod-09 via feature-flag: `route.downscale.node=runtime-prod-09`. doing a graceful drain of new sessions.

raj: proposing temporary workaround: lower max_sequence for affected model variant to reduce KV cache footprint and allow eviction. Can push a hotpatch?

leo: risk: lowering max_sequence may regress output quality for a small subset of requests. but it reduces mem pressure. give ETA?

maya: hotpatch queued, will push in 2 min for non-critical routes only.

infra-bot: Node runtime-prod-09 marked: DRAINING. New pods scheduled to other nodes.

raj: while draining, I recommend forcing an allocator compaction + a soft-evict of the largest KV shards: `allocator ctl evict --shard=biggest --percent=30` — that'll free some contiguous pages for the pager.

maya: running soft-evict now. will monitor OOM events.

sophie: telemetry after initial drain/evict: error rate dropped to 2.1%, latency p95 improved ~450ms -> 220ms. still above baseline but trending better.

support-engine: customers notified of degraded performance recovery. asking if we expect full recovery or need a scheduled maintenance window.

raj: compaction completed on node-09 but allocator reports many small free runs -> compaction didn't coalesce fully due to high resident set. we should consider node reboot as last resort if fragmentation persists.

maya: reboot is disruptive; I'd rather try a cross-node redistribute: cordon node-09 and force-pod eviction to move large-heap pods to nodes with larger contiguous free pages.

leo: agree with redistribute over immediate reboot. also open ticket to re-evaluate compaction aggressiveness for paged allocators — we may need background defrag every N hours for long-running nodes.

aj-oncall: I'm taking second-shift oncall at 14:05 UTC. summary for handoff: node runtime-prod-09 had slow kv-paged fragmentation -> CUDA OOMs -> drain and soft-evict reduced impact. current status: node DRAINED, compaction done, soft-evict run, customer errors down to 1.2%. next steps: monitor for 1h, if fragmentation returns escalate to scheduled reboot and notify customers. runbook steps attached.

maya: handing over logs/commands: ```# useful commands
kubectl -n runtime describe pod <pod>
journalctl -u runtime -f
allocator ctl status --node runtime-prod-09
allocator ctl compact --status
allocator ctl evict --list
```

aj-oncall: I'll keep watch. ping me if OOMs reappear or if compaction fails to hold. leaving a note in the incident tracker and updating the oncall log. :white_check_mark: 

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, assigned=aj-oncall, severity=SEV2, incident_id=INC-2026-0317-42.

aj-oncall: noted. will open a follow-up ticket for allocator tuning and a post-incident action item for model pin fallback paths.

leo: thanks team. postmortem if required once stabilized.
